描述_ZN: Scroll of "Two Magpies in Autumn", modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 92.1 cm in length and 34.3 cm in width.　　Self-titled: "Written by Beihong in the autumn of the thirty-first year." Inscription: "BAIHONG" square seal in vermilion. Inscriptions: "Han Huaijun" oval seal in vermilion, "Master of Foolish Interest" square seal in white, and "Wu Puhang Seal" square seal in white.　　Thirty-one years refers to the thirty-first year of the Republic of China (1942), when Xu Beihong was 47 years old.　　In the picture, there are two magpies on the thick maple tree trunk in the shape of an "S", one on top and one on the bottom, seemingly whispering, adding a bit of warmth to the sluggish autumn day and adding a bit of romance to the natural landscape. The brushwork of the tree trunks in the picture is robust and powerful, rich in square folds, staccato, and variations of lifting and pressing, showing the unique texture of the branches. The leaves are vividly drawn, with the outline sketched in light ink in the middle, and then filled in with various colors such as orange, yellow, green and green, the rich tones of which embellish the beautiful mood of clear autumn.　　This picture is painted on Duyun leather paper. This kind of paper was produced in Duyun, Guizhou, and was a kind of inexpensive paper for Chinese painting at that time. Its light yellow color makes the picture look elegant and simple, and its rough surface is not only absorbent but also not soaked with water, which makes it easy for the expression of brush and ink. During the war period when materials were scarce, Xu Beihong liked to use this kind of paper, which was between raw and cooked, for painting.
